title: Microbiology MVP - review
intro: Task-based review of the Microbiology / AMR MVP. Sign in, open Review, and work each step. Use the configured Microbiology navigation and canonical worklist and case URLs; mark Pass, Fail, or N/A and note anything confusing or broken.

steps.do: Sign in, open the main navigation, expand Microbiology, and choose Microbiology worklist.
steps.expect: The worklist opens at /Microbiology/worklist, the Microbiology navigation remains visible without covering the page, and seeded cases are listed.

steps.do: Set Workflow to Bacteriology and Sort to Newest, then refresh the page.
steps.expect: The URL keeps workflow=BACTERIOLOGY and sort=newest, and the same filters remain selected after refresh.
The filter values return to their defaults and the URL returns to /Microbiology/worklist without stale query parameters.

sections.title: Open and navigate the seeded case

steps.do: From a filtered worklist, open the seeded bacteriology case.
steps.expect: The case opens at /Microbiology/cases/<case-id>, keeps the worklist query context, and shows the specimen at RECEIVED with patient and order context.

steps.do: Use the case progress rail to open Isolates, then refresh the page.
steps.expect: The URL includes section=isolates and Isolates remains the active case destination after refresh.
The worklist returns with the previous workflow and sort filters restored.

steps.do: Record an isolate or organism on the received specimen.
steps.expect: You can add an isolate and advance the case beyond RECEIVED; the state change is reflected in the workbench.

steps.do: Enter an AST result using the seeded breakpoint, antibiotic, and panel reference data.
steps.expect: The AST entry surface accepts the result, derives an S/I/R interpretation, and does not force the reviewer into a dead end.

steps.do: Follow the interpreted AST result through review and release, then inspect the patient-facing report.
steps.expect: The released report presents the antibiotic result and S/I/R interpretation clearly. Mark Fail and describe where it stops if it does not reach the report.

steps.do: Find the sibling TB case on the same specimen, then identify the single most important missing part of the bench workflow.
steps.expect: The bacterial and TB cases remain distinct without hiding or corrupting one another, and the reviewer records one clear highest-value gap for the next iteration.
